data.details:

src/cli/commands/status.ts     | 111 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++--

 2 files changed, 210 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-)

✓ test: a journal whose last run-end carries a failed tip verification renders the failed gate by name in the status header (exit 0)
✓ test: a resume in progress after a failed tip verification renders as a re-verification in progress rather than a completed run (exit 0)
✓ test: the done-count presentation never reads as terminal success while tip verification is failed or pending (exit 0)
✓ test: a run whose tip verification passed renders exactly as today (exit 0)
✓ c1: tipVerifyPhase() folds only JournalEvent facts — run-start/run-resume (attempt count, recorded commands), merge, tip-verify-failed (gate name, fingerprint array length), and run-end.data.tipVerify — and returns undefined when the journal carries no tip-verify evidence, so no claim is invented; tipVerifyText() renders 'gate unknown' rather than guessing and omits the fingerprint clause when no count was recorded. The optimistic-green path is gated on that same journal-derived phase: when tipPhase exists the tally becomes '<n>/<m> tasks done · run not verified' with warn/fail tone instead of ok(), and the header/gauge lose their green. Nothing in the new code reads graph.json or infers verification from task completion. Tests seed real journals and assert rendered bytes, including a passed/legacy equality check (expect(passed).toBe(legacy)) proving the unevidenced path is untouched — no hardcoded-result, vacuous-assertion, or echo-not-implement shortcut applies.

data.summary: Added a replay-stable journal decision stream with exact approvalevidence and failure-isolated decision webhooks.

data.details:
1 commit(s):
src/cli/commands/status.ts            | 163 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++---
 src/drivers/types.ts                  |  33 ++++++-
 tests/cli/status-watch-purity.test.ts |  25 ++++++
 tests/cli/status-watch.test.ts        |  95 ++++++++++++++++++++
 4 files changed, 303 insertions(+), 13 deletions(-)

✓ test: a required human decision emits one machine-readable event carrying the exact approval command and an evidence pointer (exit 0)
✓ test: the stream replays identically from the same journal so a reconnecting consumer reaches the same state (exit 0)
✓ test: a configured webhook sink receives decision-tier events and its failure never affects the run or the stream (exit 0)
✓ c1: The event stream is a pure projection: decisionEventsFromJournal is a total function from the journal rows + line index to DecisionEvent[] — sequence and evidence pointer derive from the append-only line position, ts comes from the row, and no clock, cache file, or persisted cursor participates (src/cli/commands/status.ts:47-107). The only mutable bits are process-local loop variables (decisionRunId/journalCursor) that exist solely to avoid re-emitting within one watch process; on each iteration the journal is re-read via Journal.open(cwd, runId).read() and re-derived, so nothing is stored. No new service is introduced: the optional webhook is fire-and-forget over global fetch, wrapped so both synchronous throws and rejected promises are swallowed (status.ts:120-144), and it is a sink, not a dependency — the stream is emitted regardless. No new files, directories, or DB are written; the only new type surface is a plain interface in src/drivers/types.ts:11-38. Purity is independently proven by tests that assert byte-identical journal contents and an unchanged filesystem snapshot after the events run, and that a second connect returns exactly the same output (tests/cli/status-watch-purity.test.ts:106-129), plus a webhook test asserting the emitted stream is byte-identical to the no-webhook baseline even when the sink throws. Completion-faking check: none of the listed shortcuts match — no hardcoded outputs (fields are read from event.data with typeof guards and unmatched events return []), no weakened or deleted assertions (the pre-existing purity test is untouched and a new one added alongside), no vacuous assertions (replay equality is paired with concrete content assertions on type/approvalCommand), no fixture-overfit (the projection handles five event kinds generically, not the test's specific rows), no stub or TODO, and the single empty catch is a deliberate, commented no-op for an observational sink rather than error-swallowing on a load-bearing path. The tty/herdr suppression under --events (status.ts:695-701) is a necessary consequence of emitting machine-readable stdout, not scope padding.

data.summary: All three suites green (51/51) with the OBS-147 sweep intact; theattempt-1 red was solely the OBS-116/148 vitest IPC-starvation fingerprint (no failing tests), mitigated in scope bytrimming the slowed-liveness injected latency to 100ms, halving its fork occupancy while keeping it 2x the livenesswindow.

✓ test: the liveness scenario that flaked release verification passes deterministically under an artificially slowed environment (exit 0)
✓ test: no touched suite retains an assertion across a real-time bound it does not control (exit 0)
✓ c1: Each converted oracle retains a failing path on genuine regression. (a) The early-dead liveness test dropped its 5s elapsed-time bound but keeps the journal fences plus a 30s test budget against a 5-minute configured stall window (taskTimeoutMinutes: 5), so a regression that stops short-circuiting the wait cannot complete within budget and the dead-channel-failover / channel-exclusion asserts would not appear — the shared runEarlyDeadScenario helper preserves the identical scenario and assertions. (b) The bounded-settle test dropped its 10s runaway guard but keeps the discriminating fences: cause must be malformed-trailer (not stall-timeout, proving settles did not eat the 0.05m window) and summary must be UNPARSEABLE_TRAILER_SUMMARY — the staged ladder places a valid trailer at read 6, so a third re-read would consume it and flip the outcome to done/ok, failing the asserts. (c) The no-token test dropped its 4.5s bound but keeps ok=false, NO_TRAILER_SUMMARY, cause=stall-timeout, and human park; the settle-loop entry condition it was indirectly guarding is pinned by the bounded-settle ladder. (d) approve.test.ts and greenness-exit.test.ts changes are purely per-test timeout budgets (30s default → 120s); every behavioral assertion (rejects.toThrow messages, countApproved counts, exit codes 0/2, journal event data) is untouched, so those oracles fail identically on regression. No timeout was widened to mask a hang: the bounds removed are upper bounds on elapsed real time whose only failure mode was runner load, and runaway is still bounded by each test's own budget. The new sweep test is a real guard (regex over the three swept files, asserting absence) rather than a vacuous assertion, and the added slowed-latency test is a genuine second oracle with the same journal fences under 100ms injected per-call latency (2× the 50ms liveness window). No completion-faking shortcut applies — this is not test-weakening, since discriminating assertions were preserved or strengthened while only load-racing bounds were removed.

✓ test: a verdict carrying well-formed anchored comments renders them as an anchored review block in the retry prompt (exit 0)
✓ test: a verdict with a malformed or absent comment block parses exactly as today with no new failure mode (exit 0)
✓ test: anchored comments never alter the verdict outcome the gate records (exit 0)
✓ c1: renderAnchoredReview emits each comment as `- <path>:<line> — <body>` under a `## Anchored review` heading, and appendAnchoredReview attaches that block to the acceptance and review gate details. Those details are exactly what the daemon concatenates into retry feedback (src/run/daemon.ts:1380 uses the same `${g.gate}: ${g.details}` join the new test reproduces), and buildTaskPrompt embeds that feedback verbatim under 'Previous attempt failed gates' with no truncation on the path (model-lints only estimates size). The new judge-retry test drives real runGates output through buildTaskPrompt and asserts `src/retry.ts:41` and `tests/retry.test.ts:88` plus both bodies appear; I ran it and it passes. File+line naming is precise enough to act on without searching. No completion-faking shortcut matches: the fake verdict exercises the real parse/render path, assertions are substantive, and no checks were relaxed.

✓ test: the model identity is extracted from a banner captured verbatim from the live interface, borders and indentation included (exit 0)
✓ test: a banner naming a model other than the one assigned is reported as a mismatch (exit 0)
✓ test: a banner whose printed model name has no known mapping to a channel identifier is reported as unknown rather than as a mismatch (exit 0)
✓ test: the session identifier is extracted from that same captured banner (exit 0)
✓ c1: The old guard used /^Model:\s*(.+)$/m, which never matched the live TUI's bordered rows (' │  Model:   K2.7 Coding   │'), so kimiBannerModel returned undefined and confirmKimiSeedBanner fell through to {ok:true} — a fail-open on a genuinely different model. The diff strips the per-line border/margin chrome (kimiBannerLines) before matching, resolves the printed name through an explicit display-name→channel map, and returns {ok:false, status:'mismatch', error} when the resolved channel differs from the assignment; the KIMI_SEED wrapper passes mismatch through unchanged, so the generic dispatch path also fails. Tests prove it on the captured frame: kimiBannerModel(LIVE_BANNER_FRAME) === 'kimi-code/kimi-for-coding' against ASSIGNMENT.model 'kimi-code/k3' yields ok:false with the mismatch error, and runKimiInteractiveSeed reports seedFailed with runs.length === 1 (no seed dispatched). The unmapped-name path returns a distinct 'unknown' status with no ok field rather than confirmation, matching the goal's explicit carve-out that an unrecognized printed name is neither success nor mismatch; the wrapper's binary coercion is annotated and keeps the unknown status visible, and no recognized foreign model can reach a success result. No completion-faking shortcut applies: real parsing logic, no weakened or vacuous assertions, no stub.
✓ c2: The fixture is loaded with readFileSync from tests/fixtures/kimi-editor-readiness/frame-01.txt — an existing capture file that this diff does not add or modify, so it was not authored to fit the criterion. Its capture provenance is asserted structurally rather than asserted by comment alone: the frame contains the shell echo "kimi -y -m 'kimi-code/kimi-for-coding'", "Version:   0.29.0", at least one border-indented ' │  Model:' row, and no bare line starting with 'Model:' — exactly the terminal chrome that hand-authored banner strings in the pre-existing tests lack. The only derived variant (the unknown-name case) is an explicit .replace() on that same captured frame, which is unavoidable for a model name that has never been served. No fixture-overfit or hardcoded-result shortcut: the implementation parses generic border chrome, not this file's exact bytes.
